question: How does the tree covering technique differ in its application to ordinal trees versus binary trees?

sections.title: Structural Distinctions
sections.text: The application of tree covering techniques relies on fundamental differences in how ordinal and binary trees are defined. An ordinal tree is characterized as a rooted ordered tree where nodes possess an ordered sequence of children, which may be empty, allowing for arbitrary node degrees [1]. In contrast, a binary tree is also a rooted ordered tree, but each node is strictly limited to having a left and a right child, each of which can be empty [1]. A critical distinction arises in the treatment of nodes with a single child; unlike in ordinal trees, a node with a single left child is explicitly distinguished from a node with a single right child in binary trees [1]. These structural definitions underpin the specific representations and properties analyzed in the research, which define the BP representations for both ordinal and binary trees [1].

sections.title: Tree Covering Algorithm
sections.text: The tree covering technique, referred to as TC, is presented as a specific approach to represent ordinal trees [2]. Geary et al. proposed an algorithm designed to cover a given ordinal tree containing n nodes into O(n/M) mini-trees, where each mini-tree has a size of O(M) for a given parameter M [2]. This decomposition process ensures that any two resulting mini-trees are either disjoint or joined at a common root. The algorithm's focus on ordinal trees highlights the specific utility of the covering technique for structures with ordered sequences of children, distinct from the binary constraints described earlier.

question: How good are LLMs at solving traditional tabular ML datasets using ICL?

sections.title: Methodological Frameworks
sections.text: In natural language processing, in-context learning (ICL) involves formatting labeled examples as textual demonstrations to provide context to a language model, enabling label prediction without parameter updates [4]. This paradigm has been extended to tabular data by serializing table rows into text or sentences [4]. While some research explores LLMs as universal function approximators on small tabular datasets for classification, regression, and clustering via ICL without explicit fine-tuning [3], other state-of-the-art models approach tabular ICL by tuning LLMs specifically on tabular tasks [1]. Notable examples of this tuning approach include TabLLM, LIFT, and TabuLa-8B [1]. All state-of-the-art tabular ICL models share a similar task construction procedure during pre-training, where a dataset is selected or created, and a column is used as the target with a subset of remaining columns as features [2]. Inference for these tabular foundation models typically involves using frozen pre-trained weights, where labeled examples from the evaluation dataset serve as context to predict unlabeled instances [1].

question: How does multiplexing enhance data transmission efficiency in communication networks?

sections.title: Fundamental Principles and Efficiency
sections.text: Multiplexing serves as an indispensable technique in modern communication systems, primarily aimed at improving the spectral efficiency of the channel [4]. The core objective is to simultaneously transmit multiple signals over the same communication channel, thereby increasing overall channel utilization [4]. This method allows multiple signal carriers to share a transmission medium, which is particularly useful when the data volume exceeds the capacity of the medium [3]. By combining many signals into one channel, multiplexing has been a standard method in the classical telecommunication industry for increasing transmission rates [2]. The technology is widely employed because it enhances information transmission by allowing several signals to share a medium, while also reducing system costs [1].

sections.title: Core Multiplexing Techniques
sections.text: There are three basic types of multiplexing techniques: time division multiplexing (TDM), frequency or wavelength division multiplexing (FDM/WDM), and code division multiplexing [1]. Wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) increases the information capacity of optical fibers by simultaneously transmitting two or more different signals at different wavelengths on the same channel [6]. This technique requires a separate source for each desired wavelength and specific multiplexing devices to couple all signals into the fiber and separate them at the other end [6]. A significant advantage of WDM is that, because the transmitted signals are completely independent, information with different formats and data rates can be transmitted on the same fiber waveguide without requiring any synchronization between the channels [6]. WDM with low crosstalk has gained great success in offering broad operation bandwidth and increasing channel capacity [5].

question: How does the addition of XAI techniques such as SHAP or LIME impact model interpretability in complex machine learning models ?

sections.title: Methodological Foundations
sections.text: LIME and SHAP are prominent post-hoc techniques used to enhance the interpretability of complex machine learning models [5] [6]. LIME operates by building locally linear models around the predictions of opaque systems [3]. It achieves this by perturbing the input to observe how predictions change [3]. For image classification, LIME creates perturbed instances by dividing the input image into contiguous superpixels [3]. A simple linear model then learns on this locally weighted data [3]. Finally, LIME presents the superpixels with the highest positive weights as the explanation [3]. In text analysis, LIME uses an intermediate binary representation, such as the existence of specific words or image patches [4]. SHAP, conversely, is built on the Shapley value framework for efficient estimation. It calculates an additive feature importance score for each particular prediction, possessing desirable properties like local accuracy, missingness, and consistency that its antecedents lacked [3]. The main distinction between LIME and SHAP lies in the selection of the functions Ω and πx [2]. Deep SHAP extends this by decomposing deep learning predictions into feature contributions. Additionally, a manifold-based Shapley method projects high-dimensional features into low-dimensional manifold features to obtain Fusion-Shap, addressing issues of erroneous attribution [1].

sections.title: Effectiveness and Limitations
sections.text: These techniques effectively identify key features influencing model predictions [5]. By conducting detailed analyses, researchers have demonstrated the effectiveness of SHAP and LIME in improving the interpretability of decision-making processes [5]. Specifically, SHAP and LIME have been employed to shed light on the black-box nature of four machine learning models [5]. SHAP can also generate counterfactual outcomes to explain decisions when models are fed with protected and unprotected variables [3]. However, these methods are not without flaws. SHAP and LIME suffer from high instability due to random sampling [10]. LIME’s explanations often consist of highly-weighted words but provide no further information on why a text is classified in a specific manner, such as abusive [9]. Furthermore, creating local surrogate models adds an extra layer that requires interpretation for global understanding [8]. To mitigate instability, brute-force sub-sampling can be used to minimise differences in SHAP values. LIME is also combined with other methods, such as partial dependence plots, to interpret seasonal precipitation predictions made by random forest models for the western United States [7].

sections.title: Contextual Challenges and Future Directions
sections.text: There is an inherent trade-off between model interpretability and performance in complex tasks [15]. In financial markets, LSTM models face fundamental challenges in interpreting unexpected feedback dynamics [14]. Caution is required when relying solely on LSTM models for stock price prediction, as their lack of interpretability makes it difficult to understand the underlying factors driving price movements [14]. Results demonstrate that adding a feature correlated with oil stocks does not improve the interpretability of LSTM models [14]. In generative modeling, while both Neural Network (NN)-based and Bayesian Network (BN)-based models are good under loose interpretability constraints, BN-based models perform better under strict interpretability constraints [13]. KNN is widely adopted in contexts where interpretability is required because its prediction process resembles human decision-making [3]. By offering transparency, XAI enables researchers to uncover potential biases, admit limits, and enhance the fairness and dependability of AI systems [6]. Future research should focus on developing more interpretable models that are easily understood by human operators and provide clear explanations of reasoning [12]. Additionally, improving the interpretability of ML and DL models is required to ensure their trustworthiness and effective utilization in mental health contexts [11].
